svg.aria-label: How I Work. Integration: I make seperate subsystems work as one system. When I worked on my Tamagotchi-inspired habit tracker, the Synabond, I had several sensors and actuators talk to an ESP32 using various communication protocols while following two seperate state machines. Organization: I keep teams moving. This summer at Equitable I coordinated a roughly 30-person software team across UI, API, Batch, and project management through 4 sprints. I built AI agents and a Loop board that tracked 600+ leadership action items, and I stepped in as acting project manager for 1.5 weeks. Teaching: I like explaining things until they click. I worked with educators at a summer coding camp for 150+ students in Grades 6 to 10, designed a cryptography escape-room workshop, and trained the incoming project coordinator before my Equitable term ended. Leadership & Teaching. Project Coordinator, Equitable, May 2026 - Aug 2026. MES & External Liaison, McMaster Engineers with Disabilities, Sept 2025 - Present. Electrical Team Lead, McMaster Aerial Robotics & Drone Team, Feb 2026 - Jun 2026. Student Tutor, Peel District School Board Coding Camp, Summer 2024. Founder, The ArrowHack, a high-school hackathon with 60+ competitors, 2023. Beyond the Code. Outside of work, I ask the same “how does this work?” question about everyday things: why streets are shaped the way they are, what a neighbourhood used to be, and why a story landed or didn’t. I’ll happily overanalyze why a transit line runs where it does, or what the Keyblade really means in Kingdom Hearts, and I’ll explain it to you in any way that I can.
